method: Eight Mobbin MCP searches; all 27 returned previews inspected before implementation.

searches.query: Research institution hero with large typography, a scientist portrait and university affiliation
Research publications index with article titles, authors, dates and category filters
About page with a large editorial portrait and biographical text arranged in columns
Research publication archive with large linked article titles, publication years and understated dividers
University or scientific research laboratory website with an editorial typographic layout
Personal portfolio website navigation with a compact name and section links
Minimal contact footer with a large name, email address and social links
Read.cv profile with biography, experience and links on a narrow screen

decisions.observation: Cartesia separates publication dates, serif titles and quieter author lines into a readable archive.
decisions.application: Full-width publication entries separate venue and oral distinction from title and authors.

decisions.observation: Kalstore gives an original portrait and biography comparable visual weight.
decisions.application: The original portrait balances the large name; its natural blue city backdrop informs the palette.

decisions.observation: Read.cv presents biography and professional records in a compact, text-first reading order.
decisions.application: Mobile content stays in one reading column with dates and venue labels directly above their entries.

decisions.observation: IntegratedBio aligns publication labels and action targets without surrounding each article in a card.
decisions.application: Research directions use clear full-width links; paper titles remain direct external links.

design.layout: Large name and biography left, original portrait right; a blue research section; publication archive; dated news; service, talks and teaching; contact footer.
design.review: Rejected a generic centered hero and a grid of matching cards. The typography and static transport-path motif are specific to a researcher working on stochastic control and optimal transport. The motif is decorative, not a figure representing research results.
